name: The Current
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: The Grand Junction Housing Authority is building The Current, a 54-unit, four-story family rental for households at 30% to 60% AMI at 674 Durham Drive in northwest Grand Junction, the first phase of its 15-acre Confluence site, after winning 2024 Round One 9% and state housing tax credits.
why_it_matters: It shows what it took to rescue a 9% deal after equity prices fell: the housing authority paused it in January 2025, then stacked city money, two state grants, a $4.1M Prop 123 concessionary loan and a congressional grant before construction started.

status.label: Under construction (framing, April 2026); completion estimated January 2027
status.detail: Housing authority board minutes of 2026-04-14 report framing going up, a topping-out ceremony scheduled for the following week and an estimated completion date of January 2027. The authority's project page says pre-leasing begins in fall 2026 and opening is set for early 2027. No public record of the financing closing date or building permit date was found.

next_step: Watch the housing authority's board minutes and project page for completion, a certificate of occupancy and the start of pre-leasing (fall 2026).

background.text: Land: in January 2023 the city applied for a $2.25M DOLA grant, with a $750,000 city match, to buy a 15-acre site on the 24 Road corridor for the housing authority at $2,812,500; the city later said the grant succeeded and the land was bought for a planned development of up to 300 affordable units in three phases.

The Current is phase one. The first phase has to build public street access, about a quarter mile of new sanitary sewer and stormwater detention for the whole site, and moisture-sensitive soils call for pile foundations. To cut costs the team switched to a pitched roof and dropped 8 units from the south wing.

City support: on 2024-01-30 council adopted Resolution No. 07-24 committing $1.5M so the application could meet CHFA's 2024-02-01 deadline. The narrative also cites $390,000 of city pre-development money and a $757,184 fee exemption.

Stall: lower-than-expected credit pricing left a $1M gap and construction was postponed (city resolution of 2024-11-20). On 2025-01-24 the housing authority board voted not to accept any of the six lending and five equity proposals it had received and paused the project.

Restart: in 2025 the authority won $500,000 for infrastructure, applied for $2.7M from the Division of Housing, signed a letter of intent with Red Stone Equity Partners and picked Bank of Colorado as lender (May 2025), and got a $4,078,646 Prop 123 concessionary loan (July 2025). It planned to file a CHFA carryover application by 2025-11-01.

In September 2025 the authority hoped to hold a groundbreaking the week of 2025-10-20. In October 2025 staff listed what was still open: lower federal credit pricing, timing of Division of Housing funds, added state credits, a sources-and-uses gap, a congressional earmark and multiple environmental reviews. The board postponed resolutions conveying 674 Durham Drive to The Current LLLP after CHFA's commitment letter pushed the concessionary loan closing to May 2027.

By 2026-04-14 the building was framing, with Shaw building wall sections off site, and completion was estimated for January 2027 (the city's November 2024 grant request had targeted a certificate of occupancy by August 2026).
Rents and services: the housing authority expects to give 8 project-based vouchers for the 30% AMI units; water, sewer and trash are included in rent.

discrepancies.text: The state's Prop 123 announcement describes the Confluence subdivision as 360 units, while the city's resolutions describe the 15-acre site as about 300 units (or up to 300) in three phases.

September 2025 housing authority minutes say its cash contribution fell from $3,000,000 to $1,950,000 after a HUD congressional grant was added, while October 2025 minutes still list a $3,000,000 cash infusion from the authority as an assumption.
